subject: Shiny server on Mac OS X Yosemite thinks it needs Java 6

messages.author: 8e72bac5f7bfb16e
messages.subject: Shiny server on Mac OS X Yosemite thinks it needs Java 6
parts:
I recently upgraded (sic) to Yosemite on my Mac OS X machine that I'm using to run shiny server.

When I visit the relevant shiny server URL, I get a window that says "To open 'this Java application', you need to install the legacy Java SE 6 runtime."

I'm pretty sure it was running fine on my Java 7 runtime before upgrading to Yosemite.  I have a feeling that the OS is being a bit over-protective.  

Any hints on how to avoid this error?

messages.subject: Re: Shiny server on Mac OS X Yosemite thinks it needs Java 6
parts:
Thanks for your attention Joe.
You are correct:  the problem was caused by my code that requires rJava.
Turns out that Yosemite does not come with a runtime Java installation accessible in normal paths.  After that installation rJava works fine.

On Wednesday, November 5, 2014 4:21:26 PM UTC-8, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
(Not that Shiny Server is supported on Mac OS X, but...)
